title: Priority 1 – Restructure Shipping Mode Logistics
body: 'First Class' shows a late-delivery rate of 95.3%, which is +40.5 percentage points above the fleet average of 54.8%. Statistically, this relationship is unambiguous (χ² p = 0.0e+00, Cramér's V = 0.457). Recommend auditing carrier contracts, adding a secondary carrier option, and piloting expedited handling protocols for this segment. Reducing its late rate to the fleet average would lower the overall late rate by an estimated 12.1 pp.

title: Priority 2 – Targeted SLA Review for Region
body: 'Central Africa' registers 58.0% late deliveries (+3.1 pp above average, Cramér's V = 0.020). A focused SLA renegotiation and carrier scorecard process for this dimension can systematically surface the under-performing routes or partners driving this gap.

title: Deploy Early-Warning Predictive System
body: The XGBoost model achieves 54.8% recall at detecting late deliveries before they occur, with 66.4% F1-score. Integrating this model into the order-management system to flag high-risk shipments at order-placement time enables proactive intervention (re-routing, carrier upgrade) rather than reactive damage control. Even a 20% conversion of flagged orders to on-time would reduce the overall late rate by ~11.0 pp.

title: Seasonal Capacity Pre-Planning
body: Time-trend analysis reveals that late-delivery rates spike during peak seasons. Pre-negotiating surge capacity with carriers 8–12 weeks before high-demand periods, and setting conservative promised-delivery windows, can reduce customer-facing SLA breaches by an estimated 15–25% during peak months.
